title: F5 starts on Windows: the app loads async-profiler itself instead of a fatal -agentpath in every launch entry
definition-of-done:
1. On Windows, an F5-equivalent launch of a launch entry (no profiler argument) starts the scene, logging that profiling is unavailable.
2. On Linux/macOS an F5 launch writes tmp/profiles/f5-<time>-<pid>.html at exit, found by `ixdar-cli profile-report` (checked by the user on their Linux machine, or in CI).
3. `ixdar-cli run-scene` and `launch` keep profiling through their own -agentpath, and the app does not start a second profiler on top.
4. No launch entry, settings key or ixd launch-add template references java.profiler.args any more.
5. The web-teavm build compiles without the async-profiler dependency on its path.
6. Build checkstyle-green; a unit test covers the skip-when-an-agent-is-loaded decision.

Keeps LaunchProfiler's three [profiler] log lines (profiling to <capture>, unavailable here, could not write <capture>): they tell the user where an F5 profile went, or why there is none, and run once per launch.

Keeps the log line 'unavailable here, running unprofiled': on Windows it is the one sign that F5 ran without a profile.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test for the profiler start decision (agent already loaded, library found, none found). 2. Run the java command a launch entry produces, without -agentpath, on Windows and confirm the scene starts. 3. run-scene on Windows still starts unprofiled. 4. mvn compile for the web-teavm profile.
changes-made: LaunchProfiler (ixdar.canvas) starts async-profiler from IxdarWindow.main via tools.profiler:async-profiler:4.6 (Apache-2.0, Linux/macOS libraries bundled): skips when an -agentpath async-profiler agent is already loaded (ixdar-cli run-scene/launch), else loads .profiler/libasyncProfiler or the bundled library, dumps tmp/profiles/f5-<time>-<pid>.html at exit, and logs one line and runs unprofiled where none loads. All 35 launch entries and the ai-workspace wt launch-add template drop ${config:java.profiler.args}; settings.json drops java.profiler.args/off. Windows: ixdar-cli launch Ixdar starts and logs 'Unsupported platform: windows 11-amd64'. LaunchProfilerTest 3/0. TeaVM package exits 0 with 39 pre-existing-looking [ERROR] lines, none about the profiler. Not verified here: the f5 capture on Linux/macOS.
review-summary: The desktop launch now starts async-profiler itself through its Java API instead of a -agentpath in every launch entry. A missing profiler library stopped the JVM, so F5 could not start any scene on Windows, which has no async-profiler build.
